title: Behavioral, senior software engineer, average answers, coach mode

questions.text: Tell me about a technical initiative you led across teams.
Tell me about mentoring someone through a hard stretch.
Tell me about a technical disagreement you resolved.
Tell me about a project that failed or was cancelled.
Tell me about explaining a trade-off to leadership.
Tell me about a measurable improvement you made.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Nikhil, welcome. I'm Elise, a staff engineer. This is a thirty minute behavioral practice session, and I will give you one tip at the end.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Elise, thanks. Happy to be here.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What are you working on these days?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Mostly platform reliability work, plus some mentoring of newer engineers.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Good. I'll ask about three experiences and leave time for your questions.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a technical initiative you led across teams.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We had a lot of services with different logging formats, so I led an effort to standardize logging. A few teams joined and we agreed on a common library. It made debugging easier and people were happy with it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How many teams adopted it, and what did it change for them?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Six teams adopted it over about four months. I wrote the library and a migration guide. Time to find the cause of an incident went from around 50 minutes to 30, based on our incident reports. Two teams pushed back on the extra dependency, so I made the library optional at first.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about mentoring someone through a hard stretch.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I mentored a mid-level engineer who struggled with code reviews and kept getting long comment threads. We met weekly for six months. I had him review my code first, and I showed him how to write short, specific comments. His reviews got faster, and he was promoted last year. The key was making him do the work instead of me giving answers.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a project that failed or was cancelled.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We built a recommendation feature that was cancelled after a reorganization. It was disappointing because we put in a lot of work. The priorities changed and leadership moved the team. I learned to stay flexible.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What was your role, and what would you do differently?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I was the tech lead. I spent five months building before we tested with real users. A small test in month one would have shown the feature had low usage. Now I run a two week prototype test first. It would have saved about 4 engineer months.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Thanks. What questions do you have for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: How are senior engineers expected to work across teams here?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Seniors own one cross-team goal per year and report progress in a quarterly review.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That's our time. One tip: start with the scope and a number, then the story. Thanks Nikhil.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Elise. That is useful.

notes: Average for senior: scope is small and results appear only after probes.
